chicken-marketing.title: Chicken Marketing
chicken-marketing.content:
## You should sell this stuff to stupid people but call it magic.


Don't take my word for it though. Ask the Journal of Marketing. Below is an abstract from a paper published in Journal of Marketing that I think is worth reading. In short, the more you know about AI, the less you are willing to use it on various tasks. I think it's worth pointing out the conclusion that businesses should take away from this is: You should sell this stuff to stupid people and call it magic. I might be rephrasing it more than the authors would be comfortable with... but that's the weird corporate dystopia vibes that I get when I read the last two sentences in the abstract (bolded emphasis added by me)



:::example
**Abstract**
As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI’s capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI’s execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that **companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.**
Tully, S. M., Longoni, C., & Appel, G. (2025). Lower artificial intelligence literacy predicts greater AI receptivity. Journal of Marketing, 89(5), 1-20.
:::



## The lies of AI branding


The branding in AI-world is wild. There is so much humanwashing in their marketing content that it feels like buying a bag of apples with the slogan: "APPLES THAT DONT CAUSE HERPES". Would you want to eat the non-herpes causing apples? Would you be interested in some other not-super-suspicius products:


- Avocados - Totally not owned by violent drug-lords in Mexico
- Robotic Household Assistant: Infant-killing free version
- New Shirts! Buy our Limited Addition that Comes with Reduced Child Labor
- Information System Built on Stolen Knowledge Designed to Replace Human Labor - Now with less Hallucinations!


As someone who is autistic, words are really important to me. Words are maybe my favorite thing. So, when I look at the words that are used to describe AI, it feels like looking [at this awful picture](https://www.dailyartmagazine.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/04/ecce-homo-das-fresko-von-elias.jpeg). The language is wild, and obviously an intentional manipulation to create a specific behavioral response from their marks (I mean... customers). Just look at all the names of the models. They are all manipulating how you feel about the product, not what it actually does.


ChatGPT is the only exception where the model name is mostly just descriptive, probably because it was before the hype-based pump-and-dump marketing frenzy AI-boom. ChatGPT stands for Chat Generative Pretrained Transformer. The others go 100% in the other direction. Instead of calling it "Math Matrix Word Remixer Attempt #58".  It's called something to reference art, grandeur, mystical belief, or demonstrate wisdom. These systems that were built on the output of stolen human intelligence are also labeled in such a way to cover up their deception.



### Human McHumanface and their Mythical Art from Ancient History


Anthropic is one of the superpowers in the arms race to replace human output using synthetically generated data. Anthropic offers three models, a Haiku, a Sonnet, or even an Opus.  Does it seem like an accident that they named their company the human equivalent of "Boaty McBoatface"? Or their three models are named after works of art, and they are all types of art that people would only be marginally familiar with? For a company that is built on creating synthetic data intended to replace human beings, this choice was obviously intentional.


Google's Gemini was named after the astrological sign and ancient Greek myths.



:::example
**Two Chickenshits and a Chicken Fucker**
Gemini refers to two spoiled half-brothers, Castor and Pollux. The two were inseperable little shits and did everything together, including being [rapists. murderers, and sore losers.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castor_and_Pollux#Leucippides,_Lynceus,_and_death) But because their daddies were rich and powerful, they were given special treatment. When one of them died after stealing cattle from someone they lost a bet to, they asked daddy for a special treatment so they get turned into constellations instead. Doesn't seem fair to me, but that's the kind of privilege that you have if one of your dad's was the king of Sparta, and the other dad is the king of everything. The story is a rare example of heteropaternal superfecundation, which for this story mostly means a mother who was fucking a chicken and a king at the same time ([Seriously, they made statues about it](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leda_and_the_Swan#/media/File:Statue_of_Leda_and_the_Swan_-_Getty_Museum_(70.AA.110).jpg))
OK, technically she would be a swan-fucker. But this is section is about marketing, so I'm allowed to stretch the story a little bit, right?
:::


"Grok" is a word from the book *Stranger in a Strange Land* that describes understanding something at such a deep level that it becomes part of you. a deep fundamental level. From what I can tell, Grok's primary purpose is to read Twitter.


So, what does ChatGPT do? Are they stuck with having to describe their product as the generative language technology that it is? If only they could pivot their branding to something that describes the exact opposite of the product. Maybe they could find a term that ["publishers and scholars reserve the term for manuscript (hand-written) books produced from late antiquity until the Middle Ages"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codex#Etymology_and_origins) That sounds like the exact opposite of an LLM used for coding. Maybe something like that... how about Codex?


It seems like a pretty obvious marketing coverup, but I'll admit I'm not an expert. Marketing is a field I struggle with. I mostly study [supply chain fraud](https://frauddyscotty.com/research.html). But it's hard to not smell the bullshit when it's dumped on your front lawn. The marketing feels like each of these companies is a big game hunter displaying trophies of the things they plan on killing. Anthropic describes how AI might end humanity. ChatGPT will kill chat. Grok will kill deep understanding. At least Gemini is only going to kill stars and bananas at least.


The most magical part of AI is not the technology, it's the marketing. AI is a technology that being sold to us as magic, and we are told to believe it without seeing it. Why? Maybe because apparently the more you understand it, the less likely people will want to pay for it, just like buying the special edition of a limited-child-labor edition sweatshirts.
